executive_assessment.text: Island water-source differences and named 2024 flood localities deepen local exposure; Grand Moroni's reliability and affordability deficits are distinct from national rainwater dependence.
Political-instability legacies and weak water institutions constrain capacity. Proposed three-island water measures and child-protection risks are not evaluated resilience or conflict outcomes.

geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2024-09 reports: UNICEF reports about half Grande Comore's upland population relies on rainwater; Anjouan and Mohéli households mainly use gravity-fed rivers that often dry seasonally.

Source dated 2024-09-29 reports: May 2024 heavy rains flooded Fomboni and Wanani (Mohéli), Vouani and Moya (Anjouan), and Bangoi and Moroni (Grande Comore); UNDP reports 66,835 people affected across the islands and three deaths.

Source dated 2024-09-29 reports: UNDP reports KMF 77 million funded 45-day river/drain clearance and rock removal in named communities; it later reports families in Mitsoudje returned home after channel clearing.

Source dated 2025-04-15 reports: The Bank says climate impacts add to population and resource pressures in Grand Moroni, which receives most national rural-to-urban migration; internal migration accounts for an estimated 78% of city population growth.

The April 2025 PID reports unreliable, unaffordable or unsafe water in Grand Moroni, with piped distribution about two hours daily and costly tanker alternatives. Its separate 35.8% rainwater-dependence estimate is national.

Source dated not stated reports: IAWASuR aims to benefit 75,000 people (51% women) across Anjouan, Mohéli and Grande Comore through watershed restoration, climate-resilient water infrastructure, climate-smart governance and institutional capacity-building.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification or human approval. 16 of 16 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
The World Bank Climate Risk Country Profile and CCDR could not be opened; the older 2002 national communication should be treated as historical context rather than a current climate assessment.
Draft collection pending human source review and approval. IDA eligibility is not an FCV classification.
National and selected local examples do not establish district-level coverage or causal attribution.

No inspected source explicitly states that climate stress caused armed conflict or violent disputes in Comoros. UNICEF identifies potential hazard-related displacement and family separation with possible child exposure to violence; the World Bank separately reports political instability's harm to the water sector without linking it to climate impacts.
Public evidence reviewed gives island-level water vulnerability and named flood localities, but little water-access or displacement detail below island/Grand Moroni scale.
UNICEF projections are national and scenario-unspecified; the UNDP IAWASuR page reports intended targets and expected outcomes rather than verified results.
A UNICEF community-resilience article page timed out on direct access and was not used.

Main read the UNICEF projection context and the publicly disclosed April 2025 PID. Current water insecurity must not be reduced to drought alone; infrastructure, oversight and maintenance are central.
The national rainwater share is not a Grand Moroni estimate. Flood returns and intended water beneficiaries are not evidence of long-term risk reduction or peace outcomes.
